cleanIntro: A Kimber rimfire strips like a 1911 because it is built like one — bushing, plug, slide stop through a notch. ⛔ The plug and spring are under real tension and the wrench exists for a reason. Kimber asks for cleaning after every use, and at least twice a year even if it never leaves the safe.

steps.title: Unloaded, magazine out, hammer DOWN
steps.action: Clear the pistol before anything turns: unloaded, magazine removed and the hammer down. This book also sets the interval — clean it after every use, after exposure to dirt or sand, and at least twice a year regardless.
steps.quote: This product should be cleaned after every use and when exposed to dirt, sand, etc. When not in use, clean at least twice per year.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIPPING)

steps.title: ⛔ Plug depressed, bushing turned CLOCKWISE
steps.action: Depress the recoil spring plug with the supplied wrench (or your thumb) and turn the barrel bushing CLOCKWISE — toward the right side of the pistol — until the plug and spring are free. Keep your hand over it: the plug and spring are under tension and leave with substantial force.
steps.aside: Be careful, the recoil spring and plug are under tension and can fly out with sustantial force.
steps.quote: depress the recoil spring plug, with the supplied wrench,
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIPPING)

steps.title: Ease the plug and spring out
steps.action: Ease the recoil spring and plug out. If the spring does not come away easily, take the plug off and leave the spring where it is — the book comes back for it later rather than having you fight it.
steps.quote: Ease out recoil spring and plug. If recoil spring does not come out easily, remove plug and leave the spring for step 6.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIPPING)

steps.title: Cock the hammer, tab to notch, slide stop out
steps.action: Cock the hammer, then push the slide rearward until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop lines up with the semi-circular disassembly notch, and take the slide stop out.
steps.aside: Do not drop the hammer while slide is removed from the pistol.
steps.quote: Cock the hammer and push the slide rearward until the semi-circular tab on the back of the slide stop aligns with the semi-circular disassembly notch in the bottom of the slide.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — DISASSEMBLY (FIELD STRIPPING)

steps.title: ⛔ Rods from the chamber end, every time
steps.action: Cleaning rods always run from the chamber end. Wet patch through the bore, soak a few minutes, dry patch to lift the loose fouling, then a wet bore brush from the chamber end for a few passes and a dry patch after. Repeat the pair until a patch comes out clean.
steps.aside: Run a wet bore brush through the chamber end of the barrel a few passes.
steps.quote: Always run the cleaning rods from the chamber end.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

steps.title: Light oil, then a dry patch before it is fired
steps.action: Lightly oil the barrel — and run a DRY patch through before firing to take the oil back out. Then wipe the dirt off every bearing surface on slide and frame and clean the breech face and the parts with an old toothbrush or nylon brush.
steps.aside: Clean breech face and all parts (an old toothbrush or similar nylon brush works well).
steps.quote: Lightly oil the barrel. NOTE: Run a dry patch through the barrel before firing to remove oil.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

steps.title: Oil by the drop — and do NOT over-oil the rails
steps.action: Quality gun oil, not grease; shake it if it contains Teflon. The book's own list: slide and frame rails — oil, but do NOT over-oil; a small drop on the disconnector; two drops spread on the barrel hood; one on the slide stop pin, spread with a finger; oil on the barrel exterior spread with a fingertip; and one drop between the cocked hammer and the frame.
steps.aside: Cock Hammer - one drop in between the hammer and frame.
steps.quote: Slide and Frame rails - Oil. Do not over oil!
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

steps.title: Rack, dry fire, wipe the excess off
steps.action: Assemble it, rack the slide five or six times, dry fire, and wipe the excess oil off the gun. ⛔ And if it has been stored with oil in the barrel and chamber, run a dry patch through before firing.
steps.quote: Assemble gun. Rack the Slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe off excess oil from gun.
steps.cite: Kimber Operational Manual — Rimfire Pistols — Safety & Instruction Manual. ⛔ No part, form or revision code and no copyright year is printed anywhere in this book — the same gap every Kimber manual in the drop has. — CLEANING / LUBRICATION

deepAbsentReason: Kimber publishes nothing past this strip for a rimfire owner — the disassembly chapter ends at the slide stop and the next heading is ASSEMBLY. Its one stated prohibition (do not drop the hammer with the slide off) is carried both as a step aside and as a prohibition, and nothing deeper is borrowed from another source.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: ⛔ Rod ALWAYS from the chamber end
Wet patch, soak a few minutes, dry patch
Wet brush in at the chamber and OUT the muzzle before drawing back
Repeat until a patch comes out clean, then a light oil

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Breech face and parts with a nylon brush
⛔ No ultrasonic cleaning — the damage is not warranted

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Premium oil, NOT grease; shake it if it contains Teflon
Only the points this model's book names, in the drops it gives
⛔ Never into the firing pin channel
Work the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe the excess off

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Wiped clean; follower checked to slide freely

reassembly: Barrel and bushing back into the slide; slide onto the frame.
⛔ Align the barrel linkage block with the slide latch hole in the frame — check it through the hole, moving the slide carefully until it drops in.
Slide stop shaft in, then the stop rotated up to the disassembly notch and pushed inward until properly seated.
Recoil spring and plug in, plug depressed with the wrench and the bushing turned back counter-clockwise.
Rack the slide 5-6 times, dry fire, wipe off excess oil.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: the barrel linkage block must line up with the slide latch hole in the frame — you can see the alignment through the hole, and the slide is moved carefully back and forth until it drops into place. Insert the slide stop shaft, rotate the stop up to the disassembly notch and push it in until fully seated. Then rack it several times and confirm it returns to battery.
